title.value: An operator view of policy gradient methods
title.justification: The title accurately reflects the main focus of the paper, which is to cast policy gradient methods as the application of two operators - a policy improvement operator and a projection operator.
title.quote: We cast policy gradient methods as the repeated application of two operators: a policy improvement operator I, which maps any policy π to a better one Iπ, and a projection operator P, which finds the best approximation of Iπ in the set of realizable policies.

analysis.description: The paper presents a new perspective on policy gradient methods by framing them as the repeated application of a policy improvement operator and a projection operator. This operator view introduces operator-based versions of well-known policy gradient methods like REINFORCE and PPO, providing a deeper understanding of these methods. It also proposes a new global lower bound of the expected return, bridging some gaps between policy-based and value-based methods. The paper aims to enhance theoretical understanding and guide the design of new policy gradient methods.

type.justification: The paper's focus is on providing a theoretical framework for understanding policy gradient methods using operators, rather than empirical experimentation or application.
type.quote: This operator perspective opens up a new avenue of research in analyzing policy gradient methods and it can also provide a different perspective on traditional problems in the field.

name.justification: The paper focuses on policy gradient methods, which are a category within reinforcement learning focused on learning policies that maximize expected returns.
name.quote: Model-free reinforcement learning algorithms aim at learning a policy that maximizes the (discounted) sum of rewards directly from samples generated by the agent’s interactions with the environment.

name.justification: The paper is centered around policy gradient methods, discussing operator-based versions and providing a deeper understanding of these methods.
name.quote: We cast policy gradient methods as the repeated application of two operators: a policy improvement operator I... and a projection operator P.

name.justification: The paper draws connections between policy-based and value-based methods, and proposes bridging the gap between the two.
name.quote: Although several past works created connections between the two views [e.g., 11, 19], such connections are often limited to the optimal policy and they do not capture training dynamics.

name.justification: The paper recasts existing policy gradient methods including REINFORCE, providing an operator-based interpretation for them.
name.quote: We use this framework to introduce operator-based versions of well-known policy gradient methods such as REINFORCE and PPO.

is_contributed.justification: REINFORCE is a well-known existing method that is not newly contributed by the paper but is reinterpreted under the operator framework.

is_executed.justification: The paper is theoretical and does not execute REINFORCE itself, but discusses it within an operator framework.
